actualEntryInspections.headword: 御蔭様, オカゲサマ
actualEntryInspections.location: Daijisen sense 1, commonly おかげさまで, and Seisenban's grateful-greeting definition.
actualEntryInspections.observation: Expresses gratitude for others' help or kindness. A separate respectful おかげ definition includes a religious example; the ordinary social formula is not restricted to a religious belief.
actualEntryInspections.limits: No assertion that every social use acknowledges identifiable help, or that every thank-you may be replaced by this expression.

actualEntryInspections.source: Nipponica credited to 沖森卓也; Revised World Encyclopedia credited to 大野晋, on Kotobank
actualEntryInspections.location: Actual definition and word-spelling explanation; treatment of noninflecting derived nouns and exclusions.
actualEntryInspections.observation: Kana following kanji as part of the word's spelling clarify its reading. This is not limited to changing verb endings, and not every kana after a kanji is okurigana: particles, prefixes/suffixes and kana in a kango spelling do not become okurigana merely by position.
actualEntryInspections.limits: Digital Daijisen's heading appeared without its definition. Attribute these observations to the rendered encyclopedia sections, not to Daijisen. Individual spelling conventions require more than the general definition.

actualEntryInspections.source: Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten section on Kotobank
actualEntryInspections.location: Actual transitive entry, physical, restraining, securing and important-point uses.
actualEntryInspections.observation: Hold or press down, touch/support/cover, restrict motion or emotion, seize/control/secure in advance, and grasp important points. Supports the broad semantic family.
actualEntryInspections.limits: Digital Daijisen's definition did not render. Historical and specialist examples are not measured modern frequency, nor proof of an absolute contemporary 押さえる/抑える spelling partition.

actualEntryInspections.source: Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten section on Kotobank
actualEntryInspections.location: Transitive neglect definition and intransitive illness-improvement definition with classical examples.
actualEntryInspections.observation: Neglect/failure to attend is distinguished from illness improving. The latter historical use accords with JMdict's explicit dated qualification.
actualEntryInspections.limits: Digital Daijisen's definition did not render. This does not support recommending the illness use as ordinary modern speech.

御数-451255 exposed no usable definition; an ID-less おかず lookup reached a music heading and encyclopedia mentions, not a verified general food dictionary definition.

reviewEvidence.correctionComparisonProvenance: Thirteen complete families re-extracted for ten exact comparison forms after verifying both pinned JMdict hashes. Six match the original evidence exactly; seven are additional. The two unrelated ころ homographs and separate がわり suffix are not approximation or refill evidence. Applicable families are 1579080 for time-related ころ and 1590770 for かわり; the latter's refill sense is qualified usu. as お～. The ten direct guards address actual English-label overlap, not unrestricted Japanese substitution. In particular, sympathy and apology are different Japanese speech acts despite ambiguous English I am sorry; automatic operation overlaps with automation as a label. Shared tags do not establish the frequency of co-occurrence.
